name: Web Install API (navigator.install)
plain: Lets a page install another web app, or itself, with one call.
meaning: Turns a link into an install button; the user still approves. Still an origin trial on desktop Chromium.

access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: Lets a page install another web app, or itself, with one call.

limits.headline: Can offer to install a web app with one call, but you still approve it
limits.user_action: You tap an Install button on a page and confirm in the dialog
can: Show an install dialog for itself or for another web app
Turn a link into an install button
Work only on sites in the Chrome trial
cannot: Work for most visitors yet, since it is still a trial
Work in Edge, Firefox, Safari or on phones
limits.differs: Only desktop Chrome in a testing trial today.

story.what_it_is: A page can install another web app, or itself, with a single call and no menu hunt.

marketing.name: Web Install API
marketing.pitch: Lets a page start the install of a web app from a script, so a store style page can install apps in one click.

story.for_you: You click an Install button on a page, and the app installs. The browser may ask you to confirm. It is meant to make installing as simple as in an app store.
story.for_makers: Makers can build app catalogs and install buttons on the web. It cuts the steps from visit to installed app, which lifts install rates. It is in testing, so it is not widely used yet.

use_cases.example: A web game portal has an Install button that adds the game to your home screen in one click.
A store site installs its web app from a banner button.
A company page installs staff tools from a list on its intranet.
A school portal installs learning apps for students on shared devices.
A web app directory installs a tool with one click, with no store needed.
A web player installs itself right after your first listen.
A social site offers Install after you sign in, with one click.

history.change: Origin trial starts on desktop (M143 to 148, extension requested to 153)
